advances: The entire labeled actual atlas, at its full occurrence weights, is halfspace-dominated by original mixed volume. Its actual residual rank therefore has a direct depth consumer, independently of the centroid residual rank. Moreover, every actual subfamily of residual rank zero realizes an off-diagonal affine half-metronoid matching of its entire mass. Thus a centroid-dispersed but actual-affine subfamily is charged to the already accepted terminal capacity \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{aff}}(C)\), rather than being subjected to an unsupported centroid-to-actual rank comparison. This charge uses genuine canonical-stress contacts of the original \(C\). Under zero interaction they are the common endpoint contacts, and no source occurrence is discarded.
author: research-agent
proof:
All sums are finite because \(C\) is compact. Every loaded source fiber has positive volume. The feasibility in (1)-(2) is in particular feasible under the canonical stress loads, so accepted fact `1c54f5dc74c15059` gives the full labeled actual atlas and its metronoid memberships. Its labels have \(a\ne b\), and \(a,b,z\) have the same parity. Thus every opposite pair is genuinely off-diagonal and every \(m_\sigma\) is integral. The midpoint of the two endpoint points belongs to \(C\) by convexity. This proves the support assertion in (6). Aggregating equality atoms preserves the exact mass \(P_{\mathscr Q}\).

We reproduce the full-occurrence degree accounting of accepted fact `2b3bed05ecbcf74a` at the required sharper scale. If a label uses \(y=a\) as an opposite source, charge that occurrence to the source edge \(e=\{z,y\}\) paired at its other endpoint \(z\). The total charged weight on a fixed source edge is a subset of all its pairing weights, hence at most \(r_e\). The same argument applies when \(y=b\). Since the opposite sources in a label are distinct, each physical source occurrence is counted once. Therefore
\[
\sum_{\substack{\sigma\in\mathscr Q\\y\in\{a,b\}}}\theta_\sigma
=d_y(\Gamma^{\mathscr Q})
\leq\sum_{e\ni y}r_e
\leq\frac12d_y(q^\times)
\leq\frac{\gamma_da_y}{2}.
\tag{11}
\]
For the last step, direct evaluation in the parity class of \(y\) gives
\[
d_y(q^\times)=\gamma_da_y\frac{A_\xi-a_y}{A_\xi}\leq\gamma_da_y.
\]
The actual overlap construction in accepted fact `f44e38de6bcf9626` has exactly \(r_e\leq s_{i,e}\leq q_e^\times/2\) and good-class support, with the original factors \(\phi_{i,y}\) of accepted fact `179add32aa016da1`. None of those factors is replaced in (11).

Every source endpoint contact is in \(\mathsf M_{a_y/2}(C_y)\). Applying accepted fact `6769574fc1bd9f8d` at selected mass \(a_y/2\) yields
\[
\delta_C(y,x_{e,y})\geq\frac{\gamma_da_y}{2}.
\tag{12}
\]
This is one depth lower bound available at each contact; we do not add depths of different contacts in a fiber.

Let \(H\) be a proper closed ambient halfspace and write
\[
H=\{(z,x):\alpha\cdot z+\beta\cdot x\geq t\},
\qquad (\alpha,\beta)\ne(0,0).
\]
For each label whose actual atom belongs to \(H\), at least one of its two fixed source endpoint points belongs to \(H\), because the defining affine functional at the actual midpoint is their average. This implication includes equality at the boundary. Orient the label toward one such endpoint, choosing exactly one if both are eligible, and let \(R_y(H)\) be its total weight oriented toward physical source \(y\). Equation (11) gives
\[
0\leq R_y(H)\leq\frac{\gamma_da_y}{2}.
\tag{13}
\]
If \(R_y(H)>0\), the section \(H_y\) contains an actual source contact \(x_{e,y}\). When \(\beta\ne0\), (12) applied once in that fiber gives
\[
\operatorname{vol}_d(C_y\cap H_y)\geq\frac{\gamma_da_y}{2}\geq R_y(H).
\tag{14}
\]
When \(\beta=0\), the section containing that contact is the whole fiber, so (14) also holds. A fiber with zero oriented weight requires no payment. Summing (14) once over physical fibers gives
\[
\mu_C(H)\geq\sum_yR_y(H)
=\sum_{\substack{\sigma\in\mathscr Q\\(m_\sigma,X_\sigma)\in H}}\theta_\sigma
=\nu_{\mathscr Q}^{\mathrm{act}}(H).
\tag{15}
\]
If the whole space is admitted as a halfspace, its domination follows either by orienting every label as above or from \(2P_{\mathscr Q}=\sum_y d_y(\Gamma^{\mathscr Q})\leq\gamma_dW/2\). This completes (6).

The accepted audit matters here. Accepted fact `6496cb3b0fd44f9d` proves domination for a half-weight canonical stress-edge contact measure under degree \(\gamma_da_y\). Accepted fact `3f9592d2fb367884` proves domination for the half-weight pooled squared-and-residual contact measure \(\sigma^\sharp\), again under degree \(\gamma_da_y\). Accepted fact `1c54f5dc74c15059` preserves all actual labels but states individual realizations and simultaneous source-density feasibility, not full-weight atomic domination. Accepted fact `f44e38de6bcf9626` sharpens their source degree to (11), but does not state (15). Finally, accepted fact `2b3bed05ecbcf74a` proves full-weight domination for \(\tau_{\mathscr Q}\) inside its single centroid host. Its coordinates are explicitly different from \(X_\sigma\). Thus (15) is a direct stronger-scale consumer of an already accepted orientation argument. It is not an identification of the centroid atoms with actual atoms, and is not an independent new domination mechanism.

The dominated-measure residual theorem of accepted fact `be359f8a6c628483` applies directly to the nonzero measure (4), by (6). Its intrinsic base rank is exactly \(\rho_{\mathscr Q}\). Its coordinate-free residual identity gives exactly \(r_{\mathscr Q}^{\mathrm{act}}\) in (5), including rank zero and collisions. The theorem supplies \(p_{\mathscr Q}\in S\) and the bound (7). Combining (7) with the strict small-depth hypothesis and rearranging gives (8). The centroid scores of accepted fact `c1e3b8400d5b5b10` are not used to pay for (15) or (7); their definitions remain unchanged.

We prove the accepted-capacity charge (9). By the same residual identity in accepted fact `be359f8a6c628483`, the condition \(r_{\mathscr Q}^{\mathrm{act}}=0\) provides an affine map \(s\) on \(\operatorname{aff}\{m_\sigma:\sigma\in\mathscr Q\}\) such that
\[
X_\sigma=s(m_\sigma)\quad(\sigma\in\mathscr Q).
\tag{16}
\]
Extend \(s\) affinely to \(\mathbb R^n\), by extending its linear part from the base direction space to a complementary subspace. Only its values on the original base affine hull are used.

For each positive opposite pair \(g=\{a,b\}\), pool all its original occurrences separately at the two physical source endpoints:
\[
\widehat x_{g,a}
=\frac1{\Gamma_g^{\mathscr Q}}
\sum_{\substack{\sigma\in\mathscr Q\\g=\{a,b\}}}
\theta_\sigma x_{e_\sigma,a},
\qquad
\widehat x_{g,b}
=\frac1{\Gamma_g^{\mathscr Q}}
\sum_{\substack{\sigma\in\mathscr Q\\g=\{a,b\}}}
\theta_\sigma x_{f_\sigma,b}.
\tag{17}
\]
In (17), each label is ordered so that its source edge ending at \(a\) is denoted \(e_\sigma\) and its source edge ending at \(b\) is denoted \(f_\sigma\); this is only an ordering of its unordered paired edges, not a change of its contacts. Convexity of the two half-metronoids gives
\(\widehat x_{g,a}\in\mathcal K_a\) and \(\widehat x_{g,b}\in\mathcal K_b\). All labels contributing to \(g\) have the same midpoint \(m_g=(a+b)/2\). Consequently (3), (16), and (17) give
\[
\frac{\widehat x_{g,a}+\widehat x_{g,b}}2
=\frac1{\Gamma_g^{\mathscr Q}}
\sum_{\substack{\sigma\in\mathscr Q\\g=\{a,b\}}}\theta_\sigma X_\sigma
=s(m_g).
\tag{18}
\]
The weights \(\Gamma^{\mathscr Q}\) are off-diagonal and same-parity. By (11) and \(\gamma_d\leq1/2\), their endpoint degrees are at most \(a_y/2\). Their mass is \(\sum_g\Gamma_g^{\mathscr Q}=P_{\mathscr Q}\). Equation (18), with its two legal half-metronoid endpoint witnesses, makes this entire matching admissible in the exact definition of \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{aff}}(C)\) in accepted fact `8c92d1d2b1a1b7f5`. This proves (9). The accepted affine matching depth certificate also gives \(h_{\max}(C)\geq\gamma_d2^{-n}P_{\mathscr Q}\); (7) is the sharper depth conclusion at actual residual rank zero.

Finally, under \(\mathcal I^\times=0\), accepted fact `dcccecd70b052857` identifies \(x_{e,y}=x_y\) for every loaded incidence at physical endpoint \(y\). This yields (10). Every average in (17) is then exactly the common contact \(x_a\) or \(x_b\). Hence the affine-capacity charge uses the genuine common-stress contacts, with all the original occurrence mass. It requires neither a rank comparison with the centroids nor a sum of target metronoid masses or unrelated component depths. This proves every stated conclusion.
statement:
Let \(n\geq2\), \(d\geq1\), let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d\) be a convex body, and retain
\[
C_y=\{x:(y,x)\in C\},\qquad
a_y=\operatorname{vol}_d(C_y),\qquad
Z=\{y\in\mathbb Z^n:a_y>0\},\qquad
W=\sum_{y\in Z}a_y>0,
\]
\[
S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d),\qquad
\mu_C(B)=\sum_{y\in\mathbb Z^n}\operatorname{vol}_d\{x\in C_y:(y,x)\in B\},
\qquad
h_{\max}(C)=\sup_{p\in S}h_S(p),
\]
\[
\gamma_d=\left(\frac d{d+1}\right)^d,\qquad
c_y=a_y^{-1}\int_{C_y}x\,dx,\qquad
\mathcal K_y=\mathsf M_{a_y/2}(C_y),\qquad
D_y=\mathcal K_y-c_y.
\]
Here, for a positive-volume convex body \(K\) and \(0<t\leq\operatorname{vol}_d(K)\),
\[
\mathsf M_t(K)=\left\{\frac1t\int_Kxf(x)\,dx:0\leq f\leq1\text{ a.e.},\ \int_Kf=t\right\},
\qquad
\delta_C(y,x)=\inf_{J\ni x}\operatorname{vol}_d(C_y\cap J),
\]
where \(J\) ranges over proper closed halfspaces of \(\mathbb R^d\). These are exactly the objects of accepted facts `6769574fc1bd9f8d` and `1c54f5dc74c15059`. The symbol \(D_y\) is the translated half-metronoid, not a replacement for any canonical discrete support.

For each parity class \(\xi\), let
\[
A_\xi=\sum_{y\equiv\xi\pmod2}a_y,\qquad
M_\xi=\max_{y\equiv\xi\pmod2}a_y,\qquad
\mathcal G=\{\xi:A_\xi>0,\ M_\xi\leq A_\xi/4\},
\]
with \(M_\xi=0\) for an empty class, and put
\[
q^\times_{\{u,v\}}=\frac{\gamma_da_ua_v}{A_\xi}
\quad(u\ne v,\ u\equiv v\equiv\xi\pmod2),
\]
with zero entries otherwise. Assume \(q^\times\ne0\). Choose a gauge-load-minimal dual optimizer \(v^\times\) for this matching in the normalization of accepted fact `6496cb3b0fd44f9d`, and let
\[
\omega_e=h_{(D_u+D_v)/2}(v_e^\times)
\quad(e=\{u,v\}).
\]
Use its actual support contacts \(x_{e,y}\in\mathcal K_y\) from accepted fact `3f9592d2fb367884`. Thus \(a_y\) here is precisely the object denoted \(A_y\) in that fact; its \(q,v,\omega\) are here \(q^\times,v^\times,\omega\).

Let \(r=(r_e)\) satisfy
\[
0\leq r_e\leq\min\{\omega_e,q_e^\times/2\},
\qquad
r_e=0\text{ outside }\mathcal G,
\tag{1}
\]
and let \(\vartheta\) be a nonnegative feasible transverse pairing:
\[
\sum_{f:\{e,f\}\text{ transverse}}\vartheta_{\{e,f\}}\leq r_e.
\tag{2}
\]
Transverse means that the distinct edges \(e=\{z,a\}\), \(f=\{z,b\}\) have unique common endpoint \(z\), and \((a-z)/2,(b-z)/2\) are linearly independent. These include the actual positive-overlap matching and optimal pairing of accepted fact `f44e38de6bcf9626`, whose good-class and soft-cap normalizations are those of accepted fact `179add32aa016da1`.

Retain the full original atlas of accepted fact `1c54f5dc74c15059`:
\[
\sigma=(z;e,f),\qquad
\theta_\sigma=\vartheta_{\{e,f\}}>0,\qquad
m_\sigma=(a+b)/2,\qquad
X_\sigma=(x_{e,a}+x_{f,b})/2.
\tag{3}
\]
For any nonempty subfamily \(\mathscr Q\) of positive labels, define
\[
P_{\mathscr Q}=\sum_{\sigma\in\mathscr Q}\theta_\sigma,
\qquad
\nu_{\mathscr Q}^{\mathrm{act}}
=\sum_{\sigma\in\mathscr Q}\theta_\sigma\delta_{(m_\sigma,X_\sigma)},
\tag{4}
\]
aggregating coincident atoms as measures, but retaining every label in the sum. Define
\[
\Gamma_g^{\mathscr Q}
=\sum_{\substack{\sigma\in\mathscr Q\\g=\{a,b\}}}\theta_\sigma,
\qquad
\rho_{\mathscr Q}
=\dim\operatorname{aff}\{m_\sigma:\sigma\in\mathscr Q\},
\]
\[
r_{\mathscr Q}^{\mathrm{act}}
=\dim\operatorname{aff}(\operatorname{supp}\nu_{\mathscr Q}^{\mathrm{act}})
-\rho_{\mathscr Q}.
\tag{5}
\]
The centroid measure \(\tau_{\mathscr Q}\), its full-atlas exact host \(\lambda^{\mathscr A}\), and its rank \(r_{\mathscr Q}^{\mathrm{tgt}}\) remain exactly those of accepted fact `2b3bed05ecbcf74a`. In particular its atoms are \((m_g,(c_a+c_b)/2)\), whereas the atoms in (4) are the actual points (3). The capacities \(M_{\mathrm{off}}(C)\) and \(R_{\mathrm{cloud}}(C)\) retain the definitions of accepted fact `c1e3b8400d5b5b10`; (4) is not asserted to be a submeasure of a centroid host.

Then
\[
\boxed{
d_y(\Gamma^{\mathscr Q})\leq\frac{\gamma_da_y}{2},\qquad
|\nu_{\mathscr Q}^{\mathrm{act}}|=P_{\mathscr Q},\qquad
\operatorname{supp}\nu_{\mathscr Q}^{\mathrm{act}}\subseteq S,\qquad
\nu_{\mathscr Q}^{\mathrm{act}}(H)\leq\mu_C(H)
}
\tag{6}
\]
for every physical source \(y\) and every closed ambient halfspace \(H\), including equality atoms and vertical normals. Consequently there is a point \(p_{\mathscr Q}\in S\) such that every closed halfspace containing it has mixed volume at least
\[
\boxed{
\frac{P_{\mathscr Q}}
{2^{\rho_{\mathscr Q}}(r_{\mathscr Q}^{\mathrm{act}}+1)}.
}
\tag{7}
\]
For every \(\varepsilon>0\), the hypothesis
\(h_{\max}(C)<\varepsilon2^{-n}W\) therefore forces, for every such subfamily,
\[
\boxed{
r_{\mathscr Q}^{\mathrm{act}}+1>
\frac{2^{n-\rho_{\mathscr Q}}P_{\mathscr Q}}{\varepsilon W}.
}
\tag{8}
\]

Use the accepted terminal capacity \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{aff}}(C)\) of `8c92d1d2b1a1b7f5`: it is the supremum of masses of off-diagonal same-parity matchings with endpoint degrees at most \(a_y/2\) and half-metronoid endpoint witnesses whose midpoint values lie on one affine graph. If
\(r_{\mathscr Q}^{\mathrm{act}}=0\), then
\[
\boxed{\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{aff}}(C)\geq P_{\mathscr Q}.}
\tag{9}
\]
Thus \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{aff}}(C)<\varepsilon W\) implies
\(P_{\mathscr Q}<\varepsilon W\) for every actual-affine subfamily, whatever its centroid rank. In particular an actual-affine subfamily of macroscopic mass cannot be a nonterminal witness against a centroid-to-actual rank transfer.

If the canonical same-body interaction \(\mathcal I^\times\) vanishes, accepted fact `dcccecd70b052857` supplies common contacts \(x_y\) at all loaded endpoints. Then (3) is literally
\[
X_\sigma=(x_a+x_b)/2,
\tag{10}
\]
and equal opposite source pairs have equal actual points. In this case the matching proving (9) uses these common canonical contacts themselves. For general interaction it uses their convexly pooled contacts. No universal inequality between \(r_{\mathscr Q}^{\mathrm{tgt}}\) and \(r_{\mathscr Q}^{\mathrm{act}}\) is asserted.
